subject: Clarify operator proofflow & license boundary for on-prem deployment
raw_messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alan Ross <alan.ross@medsys.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify operator proofflow & license boundary for on-prem deployment

Alan —

Great to connect yesterday. Following up on the technical/contract items we discussed for the proposed on-prem private deployment. Legal asked us to capture a concise set of asks so your procurement and engineering teams can confirm feasibility. High level questions below; please flag anything that needs a call.

1) Operator access: can we agree a boundary where Redwood retains no console/operator access post-handover? If not, please specify the exact admin actions MedSys expects Redwood to retain (e.g., emergency debug, patching windows).

2) Snapshot / evidence transfer: MedSys requested an "escrow-like" snapshot capability — are you expecting periodic full VM/image snapshots, or a one-time handover of a deployable image + runbook? Also please confirm the frequency (monthly/quarterly) and retention.

3) Audit window & on-site: If auditors require an on-site access window, what level of access and what duration do you expect? Will a remote screen-share session suffice for some checks?

4) License boundary: confirm whether license is limited to specific hostnames/IP ranges or to an internal org-wide license. Also indicate whether you require explicit operator/client certificates to be issued by Redwood.

Next steps we propose: once you answer the items above we will circulate a short Order Form Annex with specific redlines for operator access, a snapshot schedule, and an evidence checklist. Lauren (cc'd) will coordinate legal redlines.

Thanks — if it's easier I'll schedule a 30-min sync with your security lead.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]
[Attachment: operator-evidence-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Alan Ross <alan.ross@medsys.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medsys.com>, Claire Ng <claire.ng@healthprocure.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify operator proofflow & license boundary for on-prem deployment

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers from our side to help your legal/engineering teams:

- Operator access: Our preference is zero persistent vendor operator access. We may allow time-bound, auditable emergency access (by exception) for critical bug-fixes. That access must be logged and require our authorized engineer approval.

- Snapshot / evidence transfer: We need a one-time handover of a deployable, tested image plus a technical evidence package (checksums, runbook, and a sample state snapshot). After handover, we prefer monthly lightweight verification snapshots (hashes + metadata) for 3 months, then quarterly for 1 year. Full-image periodic transfers are negotiable if there is a cost impact.

- Audit window & on-site: Typically we give remote auditor sessions first. On-site access is rare and will be coordinated via our procurement team; duration is usually 1–2 days.

- License boundary: License must be tied to a set of approved hostnames/IP ranges and internal MedSys organizational IDs. We will expect operator/client certs to be issued by Redwood for the initial install; future cert lifecycle should be documented in the runbook.

I'll loop Claire and procurement to see whether the monthly verification snapshots are acceptable or whether they need to be quarterly only (cost consideration). If you can provide a draft Annex with explicit handover steps and a proposed retention schedule we can review quickly.

Best,
Alan Ross
Head of Platform Operations | MedSys Health
[alan.ross@medsys.com]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alan Ross <alan.ross@medsys.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify operator proofflow & license boundary for on-prem deployment

Alan / Claire / Procurement —

Thanks for the helpful answers, Alan. Per Jordan's note I'm uploading a short set of proposed redlines and an evidence index so we can get to a specific Annex quickly. Key legal points in the draft Annex (attached) are summarized below:

- Operator access: We propose a "no persistent access" clause and narrow the emergency-access carveout to time-limited sessions with explicit MedSys authorization and two-person logging (vendor engineer + MedSys approver). Any emergency access will be accessible to auditors via the evidence index.

- Snapshot / evidence transfer: The Annex defines (a) "Initial Handover" — full deployable image + runbook + security-evidence-index (deliverable), (b) "Verification Snapshots" — lightweight verification artifacts (hashes, metadata, selective logs) with a default cadence of quarterly, optional monthly cadence at a defined per-transfer fee, and (c) retention: 1 year for verification artifacts, 3 years for the initial handover artifacts.

- Audit & on-site: We support remote-first audits; on-site access will be limited to a documented scope and require a 30-day notice and mutual WITNESSED checklist.

- License boundary: We redlined the Order Form to include host/IP-bound licenseing and require documented cert issuance for initial install; further cert rotation responsibilities can be added to the runbook appendix.

I've attached: OF-Annex-Redlines.docx and security-evidence-index.pdf. If procurement needs a cost change for monthly snapshot transfers we can capture that as an optional line item in the Order Form (non-core).

Action items:
- Alan / Procurement: can you confirm whether quarterly verification snapshots are sufficient by EOD Friday 10/08?
- Jordan / Karthik: prepare a short SOW paragraph and the optional pricing line for monthly verification snapshots.

Thanks — Lauren Bishop
Associate Counsel | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OF-Annex-Redlines.docx (document)]

From: Claire Ng <claire.ng@healthprocure.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Alan Ross <alan.ross@medsys.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@medsys.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T16:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify operator proofflow & license boundary for on-prem deployment

Lauren / Jordan —

Appreciate the draft. Procurement has reviewed the Annex and we have two quick asks before we can sign off internally:

1) Cost clarity: please provide a succinct price table for the optional monthly verification transfer (one-time transfer vs recurring fee), including any estimated egress or storage charges. We need this in a single-line item we can present to finance.

2) Escrow-trigger conditions: define a short set of trigger events for a full-image transfer (e.g., vendor insolvency, product EOL, failed remediation after 60 days). We prefer the triggers to be objective and limited.

If you can send a short updated Annex with those two items called out — we can move to an internal procurement review and target a commercial counter the following week.

Small note: please include a redacted sample evidence artifact (hash + metadata) in the Drive link so our auditors can validate the verification format.

Thanks,
Claire Ng
Senior Procurement Manager | HealthProcure (on behalf of MedSys)
[Attachment: none]
